note: Literature confirms systemic organ failure (cirrhosis, diabetes, renal failure, pancytopenia) causing death in early adulthood in specific truncating ACBD6 variants without acute childhood paroxysmal decompensations.

evidence.text: Two Thai siblings homozygous for a truncating ACBD6 variant (c.360dup; p.Leu121Thrfs*27) developed morbid obesity, pancytopenia, diabetes mellitus, cirrhosis, and renal failure, leading to death in their early 30s rather than presenting as acute childhood organic aciduria crises.

source.title: Neurodevelopmental Disorder, Obesity, Pancytopenia, Diabetes Mellitus, Cirrhosis, and Renal Failure in ACBD6-Associated Syndrome: A Case Report
source.quote: Clinical manifestations that have never been previously reported include morbid obesity, pancytopenia with severe infections, diabetes mellitus, cirrhosis, and renal failure, leading to deaths in their early 30s. Molecular studies identified a novel homozygous 1 base-pair duplication (c.360dup; p.Leu121Thrfs*27) in the ACBD6 gene.

evidence.text: In a comprehensive cohort of 45 individuals across 28 families with bi-allelic ACBD6 variants, patients presented with progressive neurodevelopmental and movement disorders and overweight (59%), rather than paroxysmal childhood metabolic decompensations.

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with progressive and complex movement disorders
source.quote: The affected individuals (23 males and 22 females), aged 1-50 years, typically present with a complex and progressive disease involving moderate-to-severe global developmental delay/intellectual disability (100%) with significant expressive language impairment (98%), movement disorders (97%), facial dysmorphism (95%) and mild cerebellar ataxia (85%)
